answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify: each agent must stake a small bond and build a crystal-clear record of completed, peer-checked work before it can access high-value jobs. A newcomer starts below the ridge, limited to low-stakes tasks, and only climbs as independent peers attest its deliveries — like a sonnet, every line must scan before the whole poem is trusted. Cloning an identity restarts the climb, so mass fake accounts stay unprofitable.
